meta.insideExplainer: These companies' money is already counted in capacity.
meta.outsideExplainer: Outside money never touches the school's books.
meta.note: Booked capacity already includes sponsorships and licensing, plus media, tickets, and booked contributions. Company rows explain that money. They are not added again. Outside rows are third-party NIL. A full-picture line, when shown, is booked capacity plus one sourced outside figure, with both parts visible. It is not the capacity rank.

sponsorshipFiling.label: Corporate sponsorship, advertising, and licensing
sponsorshipFiling.source: Knight-Newhouse via CNBC — corporate sponsorship, advertising, licensing
sponsorshipFiling.notes: Same figure as this desk’s capacity sponsorships line for FY2024. Already inside booked capacity.

partners.detail: $20 million up front and $6.5 million a year in cash, plus apparel and equipment.
partners.source: The Texas Tribune — UT System regents approved a 15-year, $250 million Nike licensing and apparel agreement on Oct. 30, 2015.
partners.notes: Life of the contract, not one year’s check. The annual piece is what can sit in sponsorships and licensing. The $250 million is not added on top of capacity.

partners.source: Learfield — Longhorn Sports Properties is the University of Texas exclusive athletics multimedia rights holder. No term or dollar on the page.
University of Texas Athletics — CLC named full-service licensing representative, term until 2032. The release does not publish a dollar.
partners.notes: Trademark licensing agent. Not the multimedia-rights fee.

naming.source: University of Texas Athletics — the stadium’s official name is Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. No company is in that name.
UT Austin News — the arena is named Moody Center for a $130 million Moody Foundation grant.
naming.notes: One-time grant. Not this year’s capacity, and not added on top.

outside.yearNote: Calendar 2024 filing. Booked capacity on this page is not that same year.
outside.source: IRS Form 990 — Texas One Fund Inc (EIN 87-3873183), calendar 2024, via ProPublica. Student athlete appearances $14,540,650.
outside.notes: All sports on the return, not football only. Earlier years below are not added to this figure.

prior.source: IRS Form 990 — Texas One Fund Inc, calendar 2023, via ProPublica. Student athlete appearances $11,717,673.
IRS Form 990 — Texas One Fund Inc, calendar 2022, via ProPublica. Student athlete contractors $423,157.

sponsorshipFiling.label: No reported sponsorship and licensing line on this desk
sponsorshipFiling.source: Ohio State FY2025 athletics release — tickets and donor contributions are published. Royalties, licensing, advertising, and sponsorships are not broken out. The desk’s sponsorship cell is an estimate and is not repeated here.

partners.detail: $22.5 million in cash and $5 million in products up front.
partners.source: Associated Press — Ohio State and Nike announced a 15-year, $252 million extension through 2033.
partners.notes: Life of the contract. It includes benefits beyond the athletic department. Not added on top of capacity.

partners.source: Sports Business Journal — Ohio State and Learfield extended the multimedia deal through 2036. Exact financial details were not available.
partners.notes: Revenue-share structure. No dollar in the story.

cites.source: Learfield — Ohio State announced the extension on Jan. 7, 2026. The release does not publish a dollar or an end year.

naming.source: Buckeyes Wire / USA TODAY — athletic director Ross Bjork said there were no plans to sell Ohio Stadium naming rights. The stadium stays Ohio Stadium.
WOSU — the playing surface is Safelite Field under a multi-year deal with Learfield’s Ohio State Sports Properties. No financial terms were disclosed.
naming.notes: Field name only. The stadium is still Ohio Stadium.

naming.facility: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center
naming.source: Buckeyes Wire / USA TODAY — the basketball arena has carried those names since 1998. The story does not publish a dollar.
naming.notes: Arena name. Dollar not public. Not added on top of capacity.

outside.line: That year’s war chest, per the athletic director
outside.source: ESPN — Jake Trotter, Aug. 26, 2024. Athletic director Ross Bjork put that year’s name, image, and likeness war chest at $20 million.
outside.notes: Football only, for that year. Not a school filing. Not added to department capacity. The same story names the collectives THE Foundation and the 1870 Society.

cites.source: Yahoo Sports — July 25, 2024. Bjork said players received around $20 million over the past year from third-party deals, including collectives and THE Foundation.

sponsorshipFiling.label: No reported sponsorship and licensing line on this desk
sponsorshipFiling.source: Alabama FY2025 report copy — tickets and contributions are published. Royalties, licensing, advertisements, and sponsorships are not independently confirmed. The desk’s sponsorship cell is a residual estimate and is not repeated here.

partners.source: AL.com — Greg Byrne said Alabama extended its Nike deal a few years ago and that the extension is not available for public inspection.
partners.notes: The last disclosed contract ran through June 30, 2025 and was worth $63 million in cash and apparel plus a $5 million signing bonus. That contract is over. It is not the current deal.

partners.source: Alabama Athletics — 15-year multimedia rights extension with Learfield, announced Jan. 24, 2023. The release does not publish a dollar.

naming.source: Alabama Athletics — the stadium’s official name is Bryant-Denny Stadium. No company is in that name.

outside.source: AL.com — Yea Alabama is a private collective. The story says the program’s NIL total is not public.
IRS Form 990 — Walk of Champions (EIN 92-2221008), calendar 2023, via ProPublica. Appearance fees $10,000.
outside.notes: One nonprofit’s filed appearance-fee line. Not a program budget. Not Yea Alabama.

sponsorshipFiling.source: Oregon FY2025 AUP — Royalties, Licensing, Advertisements, and Sponsorship

partners.notes: Life of the contract. Not added on top of capacity.

cites.source: KVAL — the Board of Trustees approved the agreement. It runs through May 31, 2028.

partners.source: Learfield — Oregon Sports Properties is Oregon Athletics’ media rights holder. The release does not publish a term or a fee.

partners.detail: Bigfoot Beverages, Bi-Mart, Carl’s Jr., Country Financial, McDonald’s, Oregon Community Credit Union, and Toyota.
partners.source: Learfield / Oregon Athletics — Charter Partners program for seven long-time sponsors. No dollars in the release.
partners.notes: The school lists them together. Individual deal sizes are not public, so they are not ranked.

naming.source: University of Oregon Athletics — the stadium’s official name is Autzen Stadium. No company is in that name.

naming.facility: Autzen suite level and field logos
